title: re-exporting an imported function names a binding rather than producing a value that escapes analysis
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': "Calling a function with unsatisfied requirements MUST add those capabilities to the caller's R row ... Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls." specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Transform-Only Builds': a build "MUST fail closed on any construct whose lowering depends on information the file alone does not carry, rather than emitting a guess" — the only normative anchor SMITHERS1802 has. Read together: SMITHERS1802 refuses a cross-module function that becomes a VALUE, because a value has no attributable requirement row; it must not refuse an ordinary CALL, because an ordinary call is precisely what a row is required to travel through. `export { count }` is an export *declaration* naming a binding, not an expression producing a value, and a requirement crosses a two-hop re-export chain intact. The reference reported SMITHERS1802 at 3:10 while the Go fork accepted it. `export default f` is an *expression* export and remains refused on both backends; that question is not settled by any sentence and is deliberately left where it was.
